text.p: French pay television compagny Canal Plus said on Friday it was maintaining its March forecast that the cost of absorbing Dutch-based Nethold would leave it close to breakeven in 1997,
"If there were to be exceptional items, this would change the results outlook," finance director Laurent Perpere told the company's annual shareholders meeting.

A company official said a planned deal with German media group Bertelsmann involving German television channel Premiere would involve the payment of a cash sum to Canal, a development that would significantly increase net earnings this year.
Canal Plus 1996 net attributable profit climbed 11.3 percent over 1995 to 741 million francs.
